nodes.label: AD-1: Chunk data authority — Qdrant is system of record
nodes.rationale: Prevents split-store drift where a chunk exists in Neon but not Qdrant or vice versa; Neon stores only user/resource working metadata.
nodes.norm_label: ad-1: chunk data authority — qdrant is system of record

nodes.label: AD-2: No rebuild on Qdrant loss
nodes.rationale: Prevents an unbounded, uncertain re-index operation after vector-store loss; zero backup posture in v0.1.
nodes.norm_label: ad-2: no rebuild on qdrant loss

nodes.label: AD-3: shikigami is coupled, not ported
nodes.rationale: Prevents a false abstraction over the answer runtime; SDK changes require an explicit change-request.
nodes.norm_label: ad-3: shikigami is coupled, not ported

nodes.label: AD-4: Single writer for the chunk lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Prevents orphaned vectors and divergent delete paths; only ingestion creates/removes chunks via filtered delete on sourceId.
nodes.norm_label: ad-4: single writer for the chunk lifecycle

nodes.label: AD-5: One embedding model, both sides
nodes.rationale: Prevents mismatched vector spaces that make retrieval silently return garbage; EmbeddingService is the sole caller of the embeddings endpoint.
nodes.norm_label: ad-5: one embedding model, both sides

nodes.label: AD-6: One shared chunk kernel, deterministically split
nodes.rationale: Prevents writer/reader/citation divergence; chunkId = deterministic hash(sourceId+position) makes QStash retries idempotent.
nodes.norm_label: ad-6: one shared chunk kernel, deterministically split

nodes.label: AD-7: Citation contract — markers validated, never trusted
nodes.rationale: Prevents hallucinated or stale citations rendering; refusal is structural because no retrieval above minScore means no chunkIds in context.
nodes.norm_label: ad-7: citation contract — markers validated, never trusted

nodes.label: AD-8: Retrieval parameters (topK=5, minScore=0.30)
nodes.rationale: Prevents ad-hoc per-story tuning of the refusal gate; retrieval scoped by notebookId makes cross-notebook citations impossible by construction.

nodes.label: AD-9: Chat history window — 7 turns
nodes.rationale: Prevents unbounded per-turn token cost and full-history loads; resolved-citation snapshot carve-out lets old messages render chips despite AD-1.

nodes.label: AD-10: Limits — one counter owner, atomic enforcement
nodes.rationale: Prevents divergent limit math and cap races; cap check-and-increment is a single Postgres transaction with a double-bump guard.
nodes.norm_label: ad-10: limits — one counter owner, atomic enforcement

nodes.label: AD-11: Notebook TTL is lazy
nodes.rationale: Prevents scheduler/infra cost for a low-frequency event; expiry checked lazily on dashboard load and notebook open, no cron in v0.1.

nodes.label: AD-12: Honest degradation scoped to AI/ingestion ops
nodes.rationale: Prevents broken/erroring UI under load and unbounded queueing; already-indexed sources and browsing remain usable during rejection.
nodes.norm_label: ad-12: honest degradation scoped to ai/ingestion ops

nodes.label: AD-13: Web search is approval-gated, never unprompted
nodes.rationale: Prevents silent external fetches on every refusal and search firing without explicit user approval.
nodes.norm_label: ad-13: web search is approval-gated, never unprompted

nodes.label: AD-14: Delete cascade order Qdrant→Filebase→Neon
nodes.rationale: Prevents orphan chunks with live citations or half-deleted resources on failure; each step idempotent, tombstone check guards in-flight ingestion.

nodes.label: AD-15: Qdrant hosting is a build decision, not a fork
nodes.rationale: Prevents two divergent Qdrant code paths (cloud vs self-hosted) living side by side; one adapter, env-driven.
nodes.norm_label: ad-15: qdrant hosting is a build decision, not a fork

nodes.label: AD-16: Streaming answers via shikigami events
nodes.rationale: Prevents buffering the whole answer before showing anything; controller pulls shikigami's token stream and forwards deltas.
nodes.norm_label: ad-16: streaming answers via shikigami events

nodes.label: Shared Chunk Kernel {chunkId, sourceId, notebookId, span, position, text}
nodes.norm_label: shared chunk kernel {chunkid, sourceid, notebookid, span, position, text}

nodes.label: H1: chunkId determinism and span coordinate space undefined
nodes.rationale: Random chunkIds let QStash retries duplicate chunks; spans measured into the wrong buffer (raw vs rendered, UTF-16) misplace highlights.
nodes.norm_label: h1: chunkid determinism and span coordinate space undefined

nodes.label: H2: AD-1 forbids the citation-render data AD-9 needs
nodes.rationale: Old paginated messages cannot resolve citation markers without either re-querying deleted Qdrant chunks or writing a Neon snapshot that literal AD-1 forbids.
nodes.norm_label: h2: ad-1 forbids the citation-render data ad-9 needs

nodes.label: H3: Removal has no ordering/atomicity across Neon+Qdrant+Filebase
nodes.rationale: A partial-failure delete order can leave stale chunks retrievable after a source is shown as removed.
nodes.norm_label: h3: removal has no ordering/atomicity across neon+qdrant+filebase

nodes.label: H4: In-flight QStash ingestion vs removal/lazy TTL orphan resurrect
nodes.rationale: A late ingestion callback can resurrect chunks/rows for an already-deleted source or expired notebook.
nodes.norm_label: h4: in-flight qstash ingestion vs removal/lazy ttl orphan resurrect

nodes.label: H5: Refusal gate races with mid-conversation removal
nodes.rationale: CitationMapper validating only against the in-memory retrieved set lets a chip cite a source removed during answer generation.
nodes.norm_label: h5: refusal gate races with mid-conversation removal

nodes.label: H6: Limits — async ingestion, retries, unowned decrements, unnamed FR-7 boundary
nodes.rationale: Fetch-on-refusal source creation could double-bump or bypass caps entirely since AD-10 never named that write boundary.
nodes.norm_label: h6: limits — async ingestion, retries, unowned decrements, unnamed fr-7 boundary

nodes.label: H7: 'A turn' undefined; SDK Session port carries unbounded history
nodes.rationale: Shikigami's Session port carries full history forward while AD-9 wants a 7-turn window; nobody is told which component owns the trim.
nodes.norm_label: h7: 'a turn' undefined; sdk session port carries unbounded history

nodes.label: H8: Source status is multi-writer; failure-reason shape undefined
nodes.rationale: Three writers (upload, ingestion callback, sources context) could mutate source.status with divergent failure-reason shapes.
nodes.norm_label: h8: source status is multi-writer; failure-reason shape undefined

nodes.label: H9: AD-2 recovery has no owner and no counter reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Recovery deletes Filebase files but leaves Neon source records ready and counters stale, with no named owning component.
nodes.norm_label: h9: ad-2 recovery has no owner and no counter reconciliation

nodes.label: FR-10 First-run walkthrough (Driver.js) — ungoverned
nodes.rationale: Driver.js appears only in the Stack table; no AD, convention, seed node, or map row governs dismissible/replayable tour state.

nodes.label: FR-11 Landing page + reduced motion — ungoverned
nodes.rationale: Testable reduced-motion-gated scroll animation requirement has no seed node or AD in the spine.
nodes.norm_label: fr-11 landing page + reduced motion — ungoverned

nodes.label: FR-12 Cookie consent + a11y preferences — ungoverned
nodes.rationale: Consent-first dependency for FR-14's cookie-persisted theme override is never ordered or bound in the spine.
nodes.norm_label: fr-12 cookie consent + a11y preferences — ungoverned

nodes.label: FR-14 Dark mode across all surfaces — ungoverned
nodes.rationale: Dark-mode AA contrast and consent-persisted override are absent from all ADs, conventions, and the Capability Map.
nodes.norm_label: fr-14 dark mode across all surfaces — ungoverned

nodes.label: In-band stream sentinel collision risk (CHAT_ERROR/CHAT_CITATIONS/CHAT_REFUSAL)
nodes.rationale: Plain-text streaming was chosen over SSE/NDJSON for simplicity until richer event types are needed; each new sentinel widens the collision surface with genuine model output.

nodes.label: SSRF DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU residual gap in snapshot capture
nodes.rationale: isUnsafeHost and the actual fetch perform independent DNS resolutions; full closure needs a custom low-level dispatcher pinning one resolved address.
nodes.norm_label: ssrf dns-rebinding/toctou residual gap in snapshot capture

nodes.label: Reconciliation Review: Spine vs Tech Stack + shikigami SDK
nodes.norm_label: reconciliation review: spine vs tech stack + shikigami sdk

nodes.label: Composite Adapter Property (weakened in spine)
nodes.rationale: tech-stack and addendum decided StorageService/VectorStore are composite adapters enabling add-a-provider-without-touching-domain-code; the spine drops the word 'composite' and this decided property.

nodes.label: Numeric Cost Limits Gap
nodes.rationale: 1-week TTL and 10-notebook cap bound only as mechanism, not numbers; 30/user and 10/notebook caps dropped entirely from spine, risking story drift.

nodes.label: ReasoningManager Omission
nodes.rationale: The SDK's ReasoningManager wrapper that every reasoning strategy must wire into is never mentioned in the spine, though GroundedAnswerReasoningStrategy is named.

nodes.label: Guardrail Omission (spine gap)
nodes.rationale: Guardrails run on every execute() and sub-agent prompts bypass once sub-agents exist; spine never mentions this and conflates it with AD-12's app-layer load guard.

nodes.label: FR-7 Approval Gate Unbound
nodes.rationale: Nothing prevents WebSearchTool from firing mid-turn without explicit approval, and nothing states approval-fetched sources must re-enter via SourceIndexer and count against limits; scope-safety hole on the product's core trust property.

nodes.label: Multi-Store Delete Cascade Unbound
nodes.rationale: AD-4 binds only chunk-side filtered delete; teardown ordering/ownership across Filebase, Neon, and counters on partial failure is unbound, risking orphan cleanup divergence.

nodes.label: FR-10/11/12/14 Ungoverned in Capability Map
nodes.rationale: Spine's Capability Map covers only 10 of 14 FRs while frontmatter binds claims all 14; walkthrough, landing, cookie consent, and dark mode surfaces have no map row, AD, convention, or seed node.

nodes.label: Qdrant Hosting Fork Undecided
nodes.rationale: cloud free tier vs self-hosted carried with no decision and no Open Questions section, despite affecting latency, capacity, and free-tier 1GB budget math.

nodes.label: Web Verification Review: chaibookLM Architecture Spine
nodes.norm_label: web verification review: chaibooklm architecture spine

nodes.label: TypeScript 5.x Outdated vs npm 7.0.2
nodes.rationale: Spine pins TypeScript 5.x under a 'versions verified' header while npm latest is TS 7.0.2 (native/Go-port compiler); flagged as training-cutoff staleness.

nodes.label: @glitch-guy0/shikigami Zero-Adoption Risk
nodes.rationale: Package is real and exact-pinned correctly but npm shows zero other registry consumers, a single-author unmaintained/breaking-change risk; recommend pin-and-lock plus fallback plan.

nodes.label: QStash 1MB Body Cap vs 5MB Sources
nodes.rationale: QStash payload limit is ~1MB but ingestion supports sources up to 5MB; if source content is passed in the QStash body it would be rejected, so the callback must pass a reference and fetch content inside the callback.

nodes.label: Deep Research / Discover Sources = Parity Not Novelty
nodes.rationale: NotebookLM's Deep Research already proactively browses and imports web sources, so chaibookLM reframes FR-7 websearch-ingest as a UX-simplified, approval-gated parity feature rather than a differentiator, spending differentiation budget elsewhere.
nodes.norm_label: deep research / discover sources = parity not novelty

nodes.label: Citation-to-Original-View Loop (differentiator)
nodes.rationale: Most tools including NotebookLM cite a highlighted-quote preview; chaibookLM instead opens the actual original resource (live page or full pasted text with the cited passage highlighted), chosen as the genuine gap and lead trust wedge versus NotebookLM.

nodes.label: Purely Neo-Brutalist Design Identity
nodes.rationale: Chosen as a brand-level, deliberate contrast to Google's clean minimalism, since there is no technical moat; execution and visible design difference become the unfair advantage.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Order Rule (memory first, tools, explicit unknown)
nodes.rationale: Ensures the agent always checks its own memory/retrieval before invoking tools or falling back to an explicit-unknown instruction, keeping answers grounded before allowing tool use.
nodes.norm_label: retrieval-order rule (memory first, tools, explicit unknown)

nodes.label: Guardrail-on-execute() + Sub-Agent Bypass Limitation
nodes.rationale: Guardrails run on every execute() call including invokeAgent/delegate aliases; the known limitation that separately spawned sub-agent prompts bypass the guardrail layer applies only once distinct sub-agent instances exist, so every current prompt should be treated as guardrailed.

nodes.label: Sprint Change Proposal: Chunk Data Authority, shikigami Coupling, backend/ Structure
nodes.norm_label: sprint change proposal: chunk data authority, shikigami coupling, backend/ structure

nodes.label: Decision: Qdrant as Chunk System of Record
nodes.rationale: Overrides the earlier lean of Neon-as-metadata-authority; Qdrant stores vector + chunk metadata together so retrieval and citation data stay co-located, with Neon reduced to working metadata only.
nodes.norm_label: decision: qdrant as chunk system of record

nodes.label: Decision: No Rebuild-by-Replay Recovery Policy
nodes.rationale: Qdrant loss is not repaired by replaying ingestion since that would be costly/complex; approved recovery is to delete affected users' Filebase resource files and surface an honest error, accepting a zero-backup posture for builder-only v0.1.

nodes.label: Decision: backend/ as Separate Top-Level Tree
nodes.rationale: Keeping backend/ outside the Next.js app tree while remaining a single deployable allows the domain/application/infrastructure layers to be extracted into their own service later without a structural refactor.
nodes.norm_label: decision: backend/ as separate top-level tree

nodes.label: Explicit Non-Picks (LangChain, headless browser, self-hosted AI, raw fetch, notebook rail)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate scope-limiting choices to keep the pipeline thin (no LangChain/LlamaIndex), avoid headless-browser complexity (JS-only pages fail honestly), avoid self-hosting cost/ops burden, enforce cache-first client fetching via TanStack Query, and keep notebook navigation simple via a dashboard instead of a persistent rail.
nodes.norm_label: explicit non-picks (langchain, headless browser, self-hosted ai, raw fetch, notebook rail)

nodes.label: Slanted Button Signature (skewX(-6deg))
nodes.rationale: Buttons alone lean right with a more-slanted offset shadow to look 'illuminated from bottom-left,' a chosen neo-brutalist signature; cards/dialogs/chips stay orthogonal so the lean reads as an intentional interactive cue rather than noise.

nodes.label: Indexing-State Shadow Loader Animation
nodes.rationale: While a Source is queued/processing, the card body stays static and only its offset shadow rotates as the loading indicator, then glows green briefly on ready — chosen so the only sanctioned glow in the system communicates completion, keeping motion disciplined and reduced-motion-friendly.

nodes.label: Typography System (Archivo Black, Space Grotesk, Space Mono)
nodes.norm_label: typography system (archivo black, space grotesk, space mono)

nodes.label: Developer Contract: Debug Component Naming (Strict Rule)
nodes.rationale: Every component instance gets a unique stable debug name shown only in debug builds via a zero-layout-impact overlay, so reviewers can reference exact elements by name while production ships with zero trace and zero design impact.
nodes.norm_label: developer contract: debug component naming (strict rule)

nodes.label: Three-Surface IA (Sources | Chat | Showcase, no rail)
nodes.rationale: Chosen to keep the notebook workspace uncluttered and unambiguous about ownership of content; notebook management is deliberately pushed entirely to the dashboard so no side panel or rail is needed inside a notebook.
nodes.norm_label: three-surface ia (sources | chat | showcase, no rail)

nodes.label: Showcase as the Signature Gap vs NotebookLM
nodes.rationale: NotebookLM shows a highlighted quote preview; chaibookLM renders the actual source itself, making the Showcase the differentiator that every flow must protect.
nodes.norm_label: showcase as the signature gap vs notebooklm
